title: Subject-Identity Removal Does Not Improve Frozen EEG Foundation Model Transfer: A Negative Result

contributions.purpose: Systematically test whether removing linearly decodable subject identity improves cross-subject transfer of frozen EEG foundation model embeddings.
contributions.mechanism: Apply Iterative Nullspace Projection (INLP) to frozen CBraMod embeddings, combined with Euclidean Alignment (EA) preprocessing and inner-cross-validation hyperparameter selection, under a leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocol with linear probing.
contributions.evaluation: First systematic evaluation on BNCI2014001 4-class motor imagery (9 subjects, 22 channels), 3 seeds; INLP-CV reaches 56.29% vs EA baseline 56.27%.
contributions.domain: EEG brain-computer interfaces / cross-subject transfer for motor imagery
contributions.source_quote: We provide the first systematic evaluation of post-hoc subject-identity removal for frozen EEG foundation model transfer, testing whether INLP can improve cross-subject generalization.

contributions.purpose: Report the negative result that linear subject-identity removal provides no benefit.
contributions.mechanism: Compare EA+INLP-CV against a strong EA+Flatten baseline and against reported fine-tuning and vanilla linear probing.
contributions.evaluation: Optimized INLP achieves 56.29% vs EA baseline 56.27% (+0.02pp, within std 7.98%); EA baseline already exceeds reported fine-tuning (53.03%) by +3.24pp; pre-defined +2pp success criterion not met.
contributions.source_quote: We report a negative result: INLP provides no benefit over simple Euclidean Alignment, refuting the hypothesis that linear subject-identity removal improves transfer.

contributions.purpose: Establish that dimension removal generally harms performance via controls.
contributions.mechanism: Run PCA-k controls removing top-k principal components and fixed INLP-10 without optimization.
contributions.evaluation: PCA-1 55.47% (-0.80pp), PCA-10 51.47% (-4.80pp), INLP-10 55.18% (-1.09pp); all degrade vs EA baseline.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct rigorous experiments with PCA-k controls and inner cross-validation optimization, establishing that all dimension removal methods degrade performance.

contributions.purpose: Explain why INLP fails, giving insight into embedding structure.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze inner-CV hyperparameter selections across 27 LOSO folds to show the optimizer self-nullifies (selects minimal iterations / weak regularization).
contributions.evaluation: 77.8% of folds select only 1-3 INLP iterations and 92.6% select the weakest regularization C=0.01, indicating subject identity is entangled with task signal.
contributions.domain: Analysis of frozen EEG foundation model embedding geometry
contributions.source_quote: We provide insight into the structure of frozen EEG-FM embeddings: subject identity appears entangled with task-discriminative signal, as evidenced by the optimization learning to minimize intervention.

self_declared_provenance.quote: To test this hypothesis, we apply Iterative Nullspace Projection (INLP) (Ravfogel et al., 2020), a method originally developed for debiasing word embeddings, to project embeddings onto the nullspace of subject-identity classifiers.
We apply INLP to a novel domain-frozen EEG foundation model embeddings-to test whether removing linearly decodable subject identity can improve cross-subject transfer.
Our negative results suggest that, similar to the findings in NLP, subject-identity information may be entangled with task-relevant signal in ways that linear projection cannot cleanly separate.
Combined with Euclidean Alignment (EA) (He & Wu, 2018) preprocessing, this approach aims to produce subject-invariant representations while preserving task-relevant information.

notes: Explicit negative result throughout: INLP statistically indistinguishable from EA baseline (+0.02pp within std); all dimension-removal controls degrade; per-subject effects mixed (4 improve, 5 degrade). Limited to a single dataset and encoder.
